title: Lightweight Origami: SDK Onboarding Playbook (Sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a small, intentionally opinionated sketch for a low-friction SDK onboarding flow aimed at engineers who need to get a Redwood SDK integration from zero to a reproducible demo in ~20 minutes. The metaphor: treat the onboarding as "origami" — a short sequence of clear folds (steps) that produce a presentable result (demo) while leaving room for additional embellishments later.

Audience:
- New internal engineers (integrations, solutions)
- Early-stage customers evaluating the SDK
- Field engineers preparing a quick POC

High-level objectives (what success looks like):
1) Developer can run a Hello-Request locally with fixtures in <20m.
2) Telemetry (request/latency/error) is visible in Console with minimal setup.
3) Integration has a reproducible smoke-test and a short checklist to hand to SRE/QA.
4) SDK pattern encourages a safe default: local dev -> sandbox -> canary.

Constraints / design principles:
- Keep steps linear and reversible — can undo a fold quickly.
- Minimal environment variables and no mandatory account configuration for first run (use local test token).
- Prioritize reproducibility across macOS/Linux.
- Provide 3 micro-labs that escalate: Hello (generate), Stream (partial responses), Embed (vectorize sample).

Quickstart (the six folds) — target 20 minutes:
1) Preflight (2m): clone minimal repo, install (npm/pip), ensure docker running (only if using sandbox).
2) Test token (1m): copy local-test-token from README/test-keys (no org signup required).
3) Hello request (5m): run the provided script hello.js/hello.py that posts a simple prompt and prints tokens/latency. Confirm success.
4) Telemetry toggle (3m): flip on the example telemetry snippet. Visit Console -> "quickstart-play" dashboard and confirm event shows up.
5) Stream lab (4m): run stream-demo which prints incremental responses — validate cancellation behavior and short-circuit fallback.
6) Smoke test + commit (5m): run smoke.sh which asserts status codes and schema of returned JSON; commit sample config to demo branch.

Micro-labs (recipes):
- Lab A: Hello (generate)
  - File: labs/1-hello/hello.js + fixture prompt files
  - Goal: verify tokens, latency, deterministic setting for sampling off.
  - Success: status 200, response contains expected stub text.

- Lab B: Incremental stream
  - File: labs/2-stream/stream_demo.py
  - Goal: validate client-side partial output handling; test interruption and re-request logic.
  - Success: partial frames received; interruption yields graceful error and reconnect works.

- Lab C: Embedding smoke
  - File: labs/3-embed/embed_example.go
  - Goal: ensure embeddings shape and consistent norm under test inputs.
  - Success: vector length matches model doc, values are numeric, stored locally in fixtures/embeds.json.

Checklist (must-haves before moving from demo -> sandbox):
- [ ] Smoke tests pass locally (hello + embed + stream).
- [ ] Telemetry events visible (request.start, request.end, error.*).
- [ ] Local test token replaced with sandbox token in env file.
- [ ] Rollout plan: feature-flagged route + canary policy documented in README.

Telemetry signals to capture (minimal):
- request.start (route, model, seq_len_hint)
- request.end (duration_ms, token_count, status)
- kvcache.hit/miss (boolean) when applicable
- stream.partial/frame_count (for streaming quality analysis)
- error.* (typed errors for fallback automation)

Gating and rollout notes:
- Canary criteria: 95th percentile latency <= baseline + 20% and error rate < 0.5% across 1h sample.
- Auto-fallback: if error rate exceeds threshold, route to a lower-capacity compatible model and send an alert to #eng-sdks.
- Rollback: immediate if smoke tests fail or telemetry shows >5% malformed outputs.

Failure modes & quick remediations (field notes):
- Local: token invalid -> ensure local-test-token file present; script prints helpful hint and link to test keys.
- Stream hang: client failing to read frames -> recommend increasing socket read timeout or disable single-frame buffering.
- Embed mismatch: wrong vector size -> check model id mismatch in config; fallback to documented default model id.

Developer ergonomics touches (small wins):
- One-liner to run all labs (./scripts/run-all-labs) that prints a short pass/fail summary.
- A tiny web UI (optional) that shows recent telemetry events for the demo token.
- Prebuilt Docker image for the labs with reproducible dependency versions.

Sample commands to include in README (concise):
- git clone <repo> && cd sdk-onramp && ./scripts/setup.sh
- TEST_TOKEN=local-test-token node labs/1-hello/hello.js
- ./scripts/run-telemetry-demo.sh && open https://console.redwood.ai/quickstart-play?token=demo
- ./scripts/run-all-labs || echo 'fix failing lab (see logs)'

Open questions (for iteration):
- Do we ship a single language-first repo (polyglot examples) or separate micro-repos per language?
- Minimum telemetry retention for quickstart dashboards — should we use ephemeral short retention so trials do not fill the account?
- Should the default playbook route users to a sandbox cluster in hosted infra or a local docker sandbox?

Next small steps (owner: Aisha):
1) Convert hello scripts to include an explicit "fold-back" undo (clear local creds) by 2025-02-12.
2) Add a tiny UI to surface telemetry events (prototype) by 2025-03-01.
3) Run user testing with two internal new hires and record time-to-demo metrics by 2025-03-15.

Notes to reviewers: this is a sketch intended to be short, testable, and opinionated. Please flag anything that feels like too much friction for a 20-minute first success path.

-- end of sketch --
